qna.value:
Training Style

"In the morning I do cardio - jogging or anything at the gym that is cardio related. At noon, I do kickboxing and around 6:30 p.m., I do ground work. After that, I swim to relax the body and stretch. I surf whenever I can get the waves and I do lots of cycling, hiking and jogging up hills."

UFC History

At UFC 46 (1/31/04), Renato made an impressive UFC debut. He dominated former champion Carlos Newton and won with a unanimous decision.

At UFC 48 (6/19/04), Renato lost a unanimous decision to Matt Hughes.

More Information

When and why did you start training for fighting?
"I've been training since 1993 when I quit playing water polo. I started Jiu-jItsu because my friends were doing it at the time. After I moved from Brazil and started my life in the United States, I started to learn different sports, kickboxing and wrestling. Everything fell together when BJ Penn started with the UFC. I became more interested in MMA to help BJ as much I could. After a while I decided to compete myself. Now, I am really hooked on this sport."

What ranks and titles do you hold?
Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu Black belt, 1996 /1997 gold medal national championship (Brazil), 1996 silver medal in the World Championships, 1998 silver medal Pan-American championships, 1998 semi-finalist ADCC (weigh-in 185 lbs and competing at 220 lbs), 1999 quarter finalist ADCC (weigh-in 175 lbs and competing at 195 lbs), and 2000 quarter finalist world championship

What is your favorite technique?
Triangle choke and sweeps

Do you have any heroes?
Andre Pederneiras, Joao Roque, Carlos Burle, Laird Hamilton, Murilo Bustamante, Minotauro and Vanderlei Silva. Mom and Dad

What are your hobbies?
Jogging and surfing."

What is your favorite movie?
Brave Heart, Pulp Fiction, Black Hawk Down, City of God.

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC?
"It's a dream to be fighting in the best organization. I'm loving it. There are no words to express how stoked I am right now. Give me more time to absorb this!"

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn?
"I studied engineering for about two and a half years, but I didn't complete my studies."

What was your job before you started fighting?
“I coached Jiu-Jitsu in Hawaii."

What is your biggest weapon in a fight?
"My brains and my heart."

attributes.title: Rex Holman

qna.value:
TRAINING: Training starts with warm-up for 15 minutes, technical stand up 3x5 minute, Full go 3x5 minute, Ground game - pick a position 9x1minute

When and why did you start training for fighting? I need to compete in a physical battle, otherwise I am unhappy. In 2005, I was frustrated with wrestling for a number of reasons. I started taking lessons from a local guy who taught martial arts. From there, I just kind of went with the flow. Sean Salmon, my wrestling training partner, began training with me and it was fun. I found new motivation to be great.  I have a couple excellent training partners that make being great realistic.


What ranks and titles have you held? NCAA Champ for Ohio State, Big Ten Champ, Pac 10 champ for Arizona State, 3rd and 4th at Freestyle Final Olympic Trials.


Do you have any heroes? Randy Couture and Fedor Emelianenko are two of my favorite fighters, although I usually come away from each event with a greater respect for at least a couple of fighters.


What is your favorite technique? My favorite technique to practice are leg kicks, I will be excellent at them.


What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? Fighting in the UFC is a tremendous opportunity. I realize how timing and luck granted me an opportunity. However, it is up to me to capitalize. I get to fight in my hometown on the biggest stage in MMA. I can't ask for any more at this point. What does it mean? I get to compete, improve myself and be successful.


Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? I went to Ohio State University and graduated with Bachelors in Business Administration-Marketing.


What was your job before you started fighting? I was a wrestling coach at Ohio State, a member of the Army's World Class Athlete Program, and am currently a Firefighter/EMT-P for the Upper Arlington Fire Dept. and an assistant HS wrestling coach at New Albany HS.

qna.value:
TRAINING: I train between 2-3 times a day. Morning at the club, afternoon on my own physio and in the evening in the club. I feel great and in perfect shape.

When and why did you start training for fighting? As a kid, I wrestled a lot in Sweden and Iran and I also became the Swedish champion. After a couple of years in the wrestling mix, I wanted a new challenge and I had some friends fighting in MMA so I said I would give it a try. Two months later I made my pro debut in Finland and I loved it. The crowd went crazy and I enjoyed it so much that I told Manos (my long-time manager) that I wanted a fight immediately again and he booked me shortly after on a show in Sweden when I actually fought for free! This is how everything started and now I am in the UFC and it really is a dream come true. I have been talking about this for a long time and there are only a couple of days left until I make my debut!

What ranks and titles have you held? Swedish freestyle wrestling champion, Swedish Greco-Roman wrestling champion, Superior Challenge title holder, X-Fight FC title holder

Do you have any heroes? God is my hero

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? It means the world to me. This is what I have been dreaming for since the first day.

UFC History

Growing up in Newark, New Jersey and Staten Island, New York, Ricco Rodriguez was introduced to fighting at an early age. His aptitude, strength and determination helped him in school sports and eventually led him to the Mixed Martial Arts (MMA).

Upon seeing the Ultimate Fighting Championship for the first time in 1995, Rodriguez became a big fan watching Jerry Bohlander fight. While Rodriguez is still a fan of the UFC, a lot has happened since the mid 90's. Rodriguez is now the Heavyweight Champion of the premiere MMA association in the world.

In 1998, Rodriguez traveled to Abu Dhabi to compete in the World Submission Wrestling Championships. He won the title in the 99+ kg weight class, defeating Sean Alvarez and Ricardo Morais along the way. With the success he found in grappling competitions, Rodriguez decided to move on to bigger and better things.

Rodriguez began his MMA career on September 7, 1999 at SuperBrawl 13. The competition was an 8-man heavyweight tournament, featuring many of today’s top stars. Inexperienced in his initial fight, Rodriguez lost to Bobby Hoffman by knockout at 3:13 of the first round.

Five months later in February 2000, Rodriguez returned to MMA competition and battled UFC veteran Travis Fulton. With the memory of the first loss still on his mind, Rodriguez dispatched Fulton in 4:49 when he tapped out due to an armbar.

Since earning his first victory, Rodriguez has won ten straight. He defeated Gary Goodridge by unanimous decision. On August 27, 2000, Rodriguez faced Giant Ochiai, smothering him and forcing a tap out at 6:03 of the match. Then, Rodriguez earned a judges' decision against John Marsh in December 2000. In February 2001, Rodriguez submitted Paul Buentello with a knee bar.

In his UFC 32: Showdown in the Meadowlands debut, on June 29, 2001, Rodriguez defeated Andrei Arlovski by TKO when the referee stopped the fight in round three due to Rodriguez's punches.

At UFC 34: High Voltage, on November 2, 2001, Rodriguez defeated the crafty veteran Pete Williams by TKO. Midway through the second round, Rodriguez took Williams' back and began to rain down punches, forcing referee "Big" John McCarthy to stop the fight.

At UFC 35: Throw Down, on January 11, 2002, Ricco took on former submission wrestling world champion Jeff Monson. Throughout the fight, Rodriguez showed his improved standup skills and finally ended the bout by TKO due to punches at 3:00 of the third round.

Rodriguez made his commentary debut at UFC 36: Worlds Collide on March 22, 2002. Ricco joined Mike Goldberg and Jeff Osborne in the booth as the guest commentator for the Pay-Per -View broadcast.

At UFC 37: High Impact, on May 10, 2002, Rodriguez defeated Japanese fighter Tsuyoshi Kosaka by TKO at 3:25 of round 2. Rodriguez dominated TK from beginning to end, slamming him to the mat and striking him continually from side control and the mount.

On September 27, 2002, at UFC 39: The Warriors Return in Connecticut, Rodriguez attained his ultimate goal by winning the UFC Heavyweight Championship. He defeated former two-time champion Randy Couture by verbal submission due to strikes in the fifth round.

After 10 straight victories, Rodriguez couldn't outreach 6'8" Tim Sylvia and dropped the title match at UFC 41: Onslaught on February 28, 2003 in Atlantic City, New Jersey.

TRAINING: I do my roadwork in the morning, have my first meal and go to my first session. The first session usually consists of conditioning or drilling. After a bit of rest and a couple of meals, I head back for my second session for grappling, sparring or whatever we are working on that day.

When and why did you start training for fighting? I started fighting about 13 years ago.  I caught a flyer for a local show out by my house in Indiana. It was kind of a dream of mine to play a college sport, and it just wasn't happening. So, I just started eating right and lifting, and I started getting into martial arts and training.  One thing led to another and by the time my body caught up with everything else, I wound up being really good at this sport.  Once I had a of couple amateur fights, I realized I was good and I ended up in the right place at the right time.  Monte Cox asked if he could manage me.  At the time I didn't realize how important that was.  He set me up with the right fights at the right time and here I am now fighting in the UFC.

What ranks and titles have you held? Former UFC Middleweight champion, IFC Light Heavyweight champion, Coach on season 2 and replacement coach on season 11 of The Ultimate Fighter.

Do you have any heroes? I don’t really have any heroes.

What is your favorite technique? The one that ends the fight.

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? When I decided that I wanted to do an MMA fight, I spent four months training.  It was an amateur fight.  My buddy, Josh, and I were training in a shed that was designed for lawnmower equipment in the back yard.  It was a little 12'x15' shed with no air-conditioning in the summer and no heat in the winter, just a little space heater.  We just trained and trained and trained.  Over the years, our training has gotten better and we've taken ourselves from those beginnings to the top of the food chain in this sport.  At the time, we were watching the UFC and we'd say to ourselves that one day one of us would fight in the UFC.  Now I am fighting in the UFC.  I'm actually accomplishing what I set out to do.

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? This everything for me, since I was a kid watching boxing to then watching the UFC. Since I started MMA after my wrestling career once done, I knew I would be here. Just had to be patient and I knew my opportunity would come and it finally did on July 29th. 

Who is your favorite fighter and why? Dustin Poirier because of who he is as a person and southpaw with good boxing. Cub is also up there because of the quality of a person he is and his dynamic style, but also the career he had and the way he helps us in the training room and in life experiences.

Do you have any heroes outside of fighting? My heroes are my parents, because of their work ethic and everything they have accomplished. Something I’m proud of and have instilled in me that has helped me in wrestling, working jobs and fighting. 

What are your current ranks in martial arts? 2x All American for CA Juco wrestling, BJJ purple belt under Erik Paulson

Specific accomplishments in pro competition? 3x LFA World Champion

What fight do you consider to be the key fight in your career? My fight against Richie Lewis because I was a heavy underdog and proved everyone wrong by finishing him in the 5th round. And I landed 234 strikes. Also, my last fight because I was able to knock my opponent down and finished him with a bulldog choke. Showed that I have killer instinct on how fast I secured the choke. 

Is there a cause that you want to use your platform for? To Represent my city of SANTA ANA and show that with strong work ethic and believe you can accomplish anything you put your mind too. I’ve had ups and downs throughout my life and wresting career but all that has modeled me to have the success I’m having in my fighting career. 

Beyond money or a championship, what motivates you? Competing with myself, being a good person and taking care of my family. I would say the most alive I fell is when I’m in that cage, and nothing beats the felling when you finish your opponent, that is something that I crave when I get a contract and a name and when I’m in the cage.

Did you go to college and if so what degree did you earn? Criminal Justice and Political Science from UNK- University of Nebraska Kearney

What was your job before you started fighting? I still work to this day on the weekends, help my dad and uncles at their Mechanic shop. Something my dad thought me since I was about 8 but didn’t start working till I turned 10 years old. I have those mechanic hands lol shout out to Primos Auto Repair in Santa Ana 

Favorite grappling technique: Choking foos out

Favorite Striking technique: Hitting them with the Zassss The Art of 8 Limbs 

Tell us about your life outside of fighting: Outside of fighting l like hanging with my family, girlfriend, friends and my dog Tyson. Working at the shop with my dad and uncles. Riding my Chopper, with my dad and the homies. Cruise around in my 68 Camaro. Snowboarding, riding my dirt bike and being outdoors. Hunting, camping, running at the beach and then jumping in the ocean. I like to Cook as well- Chef Machete

TRAINING: A typical day of training starts at 10am with team practice, and the team practice curriculum changes every day. I then have the afternoon off and I go back in the evening for private practices with the coaches or drilling with teammates. 
 
When and why did you start training for fighting? I started getting involved with MMA in the offseason of my sophomore year 2004 in collegiate wrestling just to keep myself busy but didn't take it seriously.  Had an opportunity to do an amateur fight; won it; loved performing in front of crowds; and wanted to do more.  After graduating from Southern Oregon University in June of 2007 I got an opportunity to train at Braveheart Fight Club out of Vancouver and to become a professional fighter so I jumped all over it. Started training professionally in September 2007 with only wrestling skills.

What ranks and titles have you held? I was a runner up in the 2006 NAIA National Wrestling Championships at 184lbs. For Southern Oregon University.

Do you have any heroes? My team, my friends and family that will do anything for me.

What does it mean for you to fight in the UFC? I better not screw this up! This opportunity means everything to me.  I gave up everything to fight, things such as my credit, my career as an Officer in the National Guard and my plans to teach and coach my younger brothers in wrestling.  This is where all of my team’s and my hard work pays off.  I get my opportunity to show Dana White and the world who I am and what Braveheart Fight Club is all about!  We are undiscovered talent that now will hopefully be recognized.  I am going to do everything in my ability to turn heads and drop jaws. I am very, very excited for this chance and will not let anyone down.

Specific accomplishments in pro competition? Elite Warriors Championship Welterweight Champion

Ranks in any martial arts styles: Hold no ranks, just beat up a lot of high ranks

Favorite striking technique: Hook followed by a cross
